Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-8)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $H$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot H=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}H=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}H & =U \\ {E}_{1}H & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ H & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ H & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Applying R2:=R2+2⋅R1 and then R3:=R3+(−8)⋅R1 is equivalent to multiplying H from the left by the following elementary matrices:

[100010−801]⏟E2⋅[100210001]⏟E1⋅H=U

Now, since E2E1H=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}
$$

EXPLANATION

Applying R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R1 and then R3:=R3+4⋅R1 is equivalent to multiplying C from the left by the following elementary matrices:

last_observation.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the LU Factorization Using Two or More Elementary Row Operations
last_observation.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$

To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}

feedback.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 12
question.problem:
Given that
$M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $M=LU,$ then $L=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $M$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $M$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(\frac{3}{2}){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}M=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}M & =U \\ {E}_{1}M & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ M & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ M & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Given that M=[510010−203−3] has the LU decomposition M=LU, then L=

a
[100−15100321]
b
[10015100−121]
c
[10015100321]
d
[10015100−321]
e
[100−15100−321]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix M to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to M in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

M=[510010−203−3]R2:=R2+(−15)R1⟺[100−1510001]⏞E1⋅M∼[51000−2−203−3]R3:=R3+(32)R2⟺[1000100321]⏞E2⋅E1⋅M∼[51000−2−200−6]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1M=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1M=UE1M=E2−1UM=E1−1E2−1UM=[100−1510001]−1[1000100321]−1UM=([1001510001][1000100−321])UM=[10015100−321]⏟L[51000−2−200−6]⏟U

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the LU Factorization Using Two or More Elementary Row Operations
last_observation.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $M$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $M$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(\frac{3}{2}){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}M=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}M & =U \\ {E}_{1}M & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ M & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ M & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

[10015100321]

EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix M to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to M in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

M=[510010−203−3]R2:=R2+(−15)R1⟺[100−1510001]⏞E1⋅M∼[51000−2−203−3]R3:=R3+(32)R2⟺[1000100321]⏞E2⋅E1⋅M∼[51000−2−200−6]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1M=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1M=UE1M=E2−1UM=E1−1E2−1UM=[100−1510001]−1[1000100321]−1UM=([1001510001][1000100−321])UM=[10015100−321]⏟L[51000−2−200−6]⏟U

feedback.problem:
Given that
$M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $M=LU,$ then $L=$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $M$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $M$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(\frac{3}{2}){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot M \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}M=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}M & =U \\ {E}_{1}M & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ M & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ M & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ M & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

a
[100−15100321]
b
[10015100−121]

[10015100321]

[10015100−321]

[100−15100−321]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix M to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to M in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

M=[510010−203−3]R2:=R2+(−15)R1⟺[100−1510001]⏞E1⋅M∼[51000−2−203−3]R3:=R3+(32)R2⟺[1000100321]⏞E2⋅E1⋅M∼[51000−2−200−6]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1M=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1M=UE1M=E2−1UM=E1−1E2−1UM=[100−1510001]−1[1000100321]−1UM=([1001510001][1000100−321])UM=[10015100−321]⏟L[51000−2−200−6]⏟U

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-0.5){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U.\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=0.5,{u}_{33}=1,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=0.5.$

EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix A to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to A in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

A=[−1111−310−12]R2:=R2+R1⟺[100110001]⏞E1⋅A∼[−1110−220−12]R3:=R3+(−0.5)R2⟺[1000100−0.51]⏞E2⋅E1⋅A∼[−1110−22001]=U.

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1A=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1A=UE1A=E2−1UA=E1−1E2−1UA=[100110001]−1[1000100−0.51]−1UA=([100−110001][10001000.51])UA=[100−11000.51]⏟L[−1110−22001]⏟U

Therefore, l32=0.5,u33=1, and l32⋅u33=0.5.

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the LU Factorization Using Two or More Elementary Row Operations
last_observation.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-0.5){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U.\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=0.5,{u}_{33}=1,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=0.5.$

Question 14
?

Given that A=[12−1250−1−23] has the LU decomposition A=LU, then L=

a
[100310−241]
b
[100−210−101]
c
[100210−101]
d
[100210101]
e
[100010−131]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix A to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to A in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

A=[12−1250−1−23]R2:=R2+(−2)R1⟺[100−210001]⏞E1⋅A∼[12−1012−1−23]R3:=R3+R1⟺[100010101]⏞E2⋅E1⋅A∼[12−1012002]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1A=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1A=UE1A=E2−1UA=E1−1E2−1UA=[100−210001]−1[100010101]−1UA=([100210001][100010−101])UA=[100210−101]⏟L[12−1012002]⏟U

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the LU Factorization Using Two or More Elementary Row Operations
last_observation.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix A to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to A in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

feedback.name: Question 14
feedback.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -4 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -4 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Given that A=[−11−43−56011] has the LU decomposition A=LU, then l32⋅u33=

a
2
b
1
c
−1
d
−12
e
12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix A to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to A in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

A=[−11−43−56011]R2:=R2+3R1⟺[100310001]⏞E1⋅A∼[−11−40−2−6011]R3:=R3+12R2⟺[1000100121]⏞E2⋅E1⋅A∼[−11−40−2−600−2]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E2E1A=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E2E1A=UE1A=E2−1UA=E1−1E2−1UA=[100310001]−1[1000100121]−1UA=([100−310001][1000100−121])UA=[100−3100−121]⏟L[−11−40−2−600−2]⏟U

Therefore, l32=−12,u33=−2, and l32⋅u33=1.
